Genital Tract Infection.question: 1) The most common sexually transmitted bacterial infection worldwide is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Chlamydia trachomatis is the most common bacterial STI and is frequently asymptomatic.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 2) The most common causative organism of pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: PID is usually polymicrobial, with gonorrhea and chlamydia being the principal pathogens.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 3) The most common presenting symptom of pelvic inflammatory disease is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Lower abdominal or pelvic pain is the hallmark symptom of PID.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 4) Cervical motion tenderness is a characteristic finding in:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Cervical motion tenderness is one of the minimum clinical criteria for diagnosing PID.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 5) The most common long-term complication of PID is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Tubal scarring following PID is a major cause of infertility.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 6) The investigation of choice for diagnosing gonorrhea and chlamydial infection is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: NAAT is the most sensitive and specific diagnostic test.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 7) The recommended first-line treatment for uncomplicated gonorrhea includes:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Ceftriaxone is the first-line antibiotic for uncomplicated gonococcal infection.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 8) The drug of choice for uncomplicated chlamydial infection in a non-pregnant woman is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Doxycycline is recommended as first-line therapy for uncomplicated chlamydial infection.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 9) Which sexually transmitted infection is characterized by a painless genital ulcer?
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Primary syphilis classically presents with a painless chancre.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 10) Painful grouped vesicles on the vulva are characteristic of:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: HSV infection presents with painful vesicles that ulcerate.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 11) The causative organism of genital herpes is most commonly:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: HSV-2 is the commonest cause of genital herpes, although HSV-1 is increasingly recognized.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 12) The drug of choice for primary genital herpes is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Oral acyclovir reduces symptom duration and viral shedding.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 13) The causative organism of chancroid is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Chancroid presents with painful soft genital ulcers.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 14) The classical lesion of primary syphilis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: A hard, painless chancre is the hallmark of primary syphilis.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 15) The screening test most commonly used for syphilis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: VDRL is commonly used for screening; treponemal tests confirm the diagnosis.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 16) A 23-year-old woman presents with bilateral lower abdominal pain, fever, mucopurulent cervical discharge, and cervical motion tenderness. The most likely diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Fever, pelvic pain, discharge, and cervical motion tenderness strongly suggest PID.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 17) A sexually active woman presents with dysuria and mucopurulent endocervical discharge. NAAT is positive for Chlamydia trachomatis. The most likely complication if untreated is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Untreated chlamydial infection can progress to PID and tubal damage.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 18) A woman presents with a painless genital ulcer and non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. The most likely diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: A painless chancre with painless lymphadenopathy is typical of syphilis.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 19) A woman presents with painful genital ulcers and tender inguinal lymph nodes. Multiple vesicles were present before ulceration. The most likely diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Painful vesicles progressing to ulcers are characteristic of HSV infection.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 20) A woman presents with a painful ragged genital ulcer and tender suppurative inguinal lymph nodes (bubo). The most likely diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Chancroid classically presents with painful soft chancres and painful buboes.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 21) The most common cause of genital warts is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Low-risk HPV types 6 and 11 are responsible for most genital warts.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 22) The HPV types most strongly associated with cervical cancer are:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: HPV 16 and 18 are high-risk oncogenic types responsible for most cervical cancers.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 23) The most important preventive measure against HPV-related cervical disease is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: HPV vaccination significantly reduces HPV infection and cervical precancerous lesions.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 24) A woman complains of a dragging sensation in the vagina and a mass protruding during straining. The most likely diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: A vaginal bulge with a dragging sensation is characteristic of pelvic organ prolapse.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 25) The most important risk factor for pelvic organ prolapse is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Repeated vaginal childbirth weakens the pelvic floor and is the strongest risk factor for prolapse.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 26) The most common pathogen causing tubo-ovarian abscess is:
Genital Tract Infection.option3: Polymicrobial infection (including N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis)
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Tubo-ovarian abscess is usually a polymicrobial complication of PID.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 27) The most important investigation to exclude pregnancy before diagnosing PID is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Ectopic pregnancy can mimic PID and must be excluded first.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 28) The most common cause of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is perihepatitis associated mainly with chlamydial PID.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 29) The characteristic laparoscopic finding in Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Fibrous adhesions between the liver capsule and anterior abdominal wall are typical.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 30) The major cause of infertility following PID is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Tubal fibrosis and obstruction are responsible for infertility after PID.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 31) The first-line outpatient treatment for mild PID should include coverage for:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: PID treatment should provide broad-spectrum antimicrobial coverage.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 32) Which patient with PID requires hospitalization?
Genital Tract Infection.option1: Unable to exclude surgical emergency or severe illness
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Severe PID, pregnancy, tubo-ovarian abscess, or uncertain diagnosis are indications for admission.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 33) The recommended management of sexual partners of women with chlamydial infection is:
Genital Tract Infection.option1: Evaluation and treatment regardless of symptoms
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Treating partners prevents reinfection and further transmission.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 34) The causative organism of lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: LGV is caused by invasive L1, L2, and L3 serovars of C. trachomatis.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 35) The causative organism of granuloma inguinale (donovanosis) is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Donovanosis is caused by Klebsiella granulomatis (formerly Calymmatobacterium granulomatis).

Genital Tract Infection.question: 36) A sexually active woman presents with pelvic pain, fever, and cervical motion tenderness. Pregnancy test is negative. The most likely diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: This combination fulfills the minimum clinical criteria for PID.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 37) A woman with PID continues to deteriorate despite 72 hours of intravenous antibiotics. Ultrasound shows a large tubo-ovarian abscess. The next step is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Persistent abscess despite antibiotics requires drainage or surgery.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 38) A woman presents with recurrent ectopic pregnancy after previous PID. The underlying mechanism is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Tubal damage increases the risk of ectopic implantation.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 39) A patient presents with multiple cauliflower-like vulval lesions. The most likely diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: HPV 6 and 11 produce exophytic genital warts.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 40) The first-line treatment for external genital warts includes:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Podophyllotoxin is commonly used for external genital warts but is contraindicated during pregnancy.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 41) A woman presents with urinary leakage during coughing and sneezing. The most likely diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Leakage with raised intra-abdominal pressure is typical of stress incontinence.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 42) The most common cause of stress urinary incontinence in women is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Childbirth and pelvic floor damage weaken urethral support.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 43) The first-line treatment for mild stress urinary incontinence is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Conservative management is the initial treatment.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 44) A woman experiences a sudden compelling desire to void followed immediately by urine leakage. The diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Urge incontinence is caused by involuntary detrusor contractions.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 45) The most common cause of urge urinary incontinence is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Overactive bladder is characterized by involuntary detrusor contractions.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 46) A multiparous woman complains of a mass protruding beyond the introitus. The cervix is completely outside the vagina. The diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Procidentia refers to complete uterine prolapse beyond the vaginal introitus.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 47) The most common compartment involved in anterior vaginal wall prolapse is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Cystocele results from weakness of the anterior vaginal wall supporting the bladder.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 48) A woman complains of difficulty with defecation and needs to press the posterior vaginal wall to empty her bowel. The diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Rectocele commonly causes obstructed defecation and vaginal splinting.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 49) A 65-year-old woman with severe uterine prolapse has completed childbearing and is fit for surgery. The definitive treatment is:
Genital Tract Infection.option1: Vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Definitive management of advanced prolapse is vaginal hysterectomy with appropriate repair.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 50) A frail 82-year-old woman with symptomatic uterine prolapse is not fit for surgery. The most appropriate management is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: A vaginal pessary provides effective conservative management in women unsuitable for surgery.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 51) The most common cause of vesicovaginal fistula (VVF) in developing countries is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Prolonged obstructed labor causes ischemic necrosis between the bladder and vagina, leading to VVF.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 52) The most common cause of vesicovaginal fistula in developed countries is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Iatrogenic injury during pelvic surgery is the leading cause in developed countries.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 53) The cardinal symptom of vesicovaginal fistula is:
Genital Tract Infection.option3: Continuous leakage of urine through the vagina
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Continuous painless urinary leakage is the hallmark of VVF.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 54) The simplest bedside test to confirm vesicovaginal fistula is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Instillation of methylene blue into the bladder confirms urinary leakage through the fistula.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 55) The most common cause of rectovaginal fistula is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Third- and fourth-degree perineal tears are the commonest causes.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 56) The commonest symptom of rectovaginal fistula is:
Genital Tract Infection.option3: Passage of flatus and feces through the vagina
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Passage of feces or flatus per vagina is diagnostic.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 57) The first-line treatment for mild pelvic organ prolapse in women wishing to avoid surgery is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Kegel exercises improve pelvic floor strength and symptoms.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 58) The main support of the uterus preventing uterine prolapse is provided by the:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Level I support of DeLancey consists mainly of the uterosacral and cardinal ligaments.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 59) Which compartment defect produces an enterocele?
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Enterocele results from herniation of the pouch of Douglas into the upper vagina.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 60) The most common symptom of cystocele is:
Genital Tract Infection.option2: Urinary symptoms with a vaginal bulge
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Frequency, incomplete emptying, and vaginal bulging are common.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 61) A 30-year-old woman presents with fever, lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness, and a positive NAAT for Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Her husband is asymptomatic. The most appropriate advice is:
Genital Tract Infection.option2: Repeat NAAT after one month before treating
Genital Tract Infection.option3: No treatment is needed for the husband
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Sexual partners require evaluation and treatment to prevent reinfection.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 62) A woman presents with a painless beefy-red ulcer that bleeds easily on touch. The most likely diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Donovanosis produces painless, beefy-red, highly vascular ulcers.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 63) A woman with recurrent PID is most likely to develop which complication?
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Chronic pelvic pain is a frequent long-term consequence of recurrent PID.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 64) A patient presents with painful genital ulcers and tender inguinal buboes. Gram stain shows school-of-fish arrangement of gram-negative coccobacilli. The diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Haemophilus ducreyi causes painful soft chancres with tender buboes.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 65) A woman with genital herpes in late pregnancy develops active genital lesions during labor. The preferred mode of delivery is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Cesarean delivery reduces neonatal HSV transmission when active lesions are present.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 66) A 52-year-old woman complains of a vaginal bulge and urinary frequency. Examination reveals descent of the bladder through the anterior vaginal wall. The diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Herniation of the bladder into the anterior vaginal wall is a cystocele.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 67) A woman complains of fecal incontinence and passage of stool through the vagina following prolonged labor. The diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Obstetric trauma is the commonest cause of rectovaginal fistula.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 68) A patient presents with continuous urinary leakage after abdominal hysterectomy. Which diagnosis should be suspected first?
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Continuous leakage after pelvic surgery strongly suggests VVF.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 69) A woman with pelvic organ prolapse wishes to preserve fertility. Which surgical option is most appropriate?
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Fertility-preserving reconstructive procedures are preferred in women desiring future pregnancy.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 70) A woman with stress urinary incontinence has persistent symptoms despite adequate pelvic floor exercises. The most appropriate definitive treatment is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Mid-urethral sling surgery is the standard surgical treatment for persistent stress urinary incontinence.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 71) A woman presents with pelvic pressure and a vaginal bulge. Examination shows descent of the vaginal apex after previous hysterectomy. The diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Vaginal vault prolapse occurs after hysterectomy due to apical support failure.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 72) A patient with genital warts asks whether the causative HPV types are the same ones that most commonly cause cervical cancer. The correct response is:
Genital Tract Infection.option2: Yes, HPV 6 and 11 cause most cervical cancers
Genital Tract Infection.option3: HPV has no association with cervical cancer
Genital Tract Infection.option4: No, HPV 16 and 18 are the major oncogenic types
Genital Tract Infection.exp: HPV 6 and 11 cause most genital warts, whereas HPV 16 and 18 account for most cervical cancers.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 73) A woman with PID undergoes pregnancy testing, which is positive. She has severe unilateral pain and cervical motion tenderness. The diagnosis that must be excluded urgently is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Ectopic pregnancy can closely mimic PID and is potentially life-threatening.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 74) A woman with symptomatic uterine prolapse also has a large cystocele and rectocele. She has completed childbearing. The most appropriate definitive management is:
Genital Tract Infection.option4: Vaginal hysterectomy with anterior and posterior colporrhaphy
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Combined pelvic floor repair addresses multicompartment prolapse.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 75) A woman presents with recurrent genital herpes. Which feature distinguishes recurrent infection from primary infection?
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Recurrent HSV infections are typically milder and resolve more rapidly than primary episodes.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 76) The most common complication of untreated chlamydial cervicitis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Ascending chlamydial infection commonly leads to PID, increasing the risk of infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 77) The most common organism causing Bartholin gland abscess is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Bartholin abscesses are usually polymicrobial, with E. coli being the commonest isolate.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 78) The treatment of a symptomatic Bartholin gland abscess is:
Genital Tract Infection.option2: Incision and drainage with Word catheter or marsupialization
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Drainage with continuous drainage or marsupialization is preferred to reduce recurrence.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 79) The most common symptom of a Bartholin cyst is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: A Bartholin cyst is usually painless unless it becomes infected.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 80) The organism responsible for bacterial vaginosis produces a characteristic odor because of:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Anaerobic bacteria produce volatile amines, causing the characteristic fishy odor.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 81) A 26-year-old woman presents with a painful unilateral vulval swelling associated with fever and difficulty walking. The most likely diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Painful tender swelling of the posterolateral vulva with fever suggests a Bartholin abscess.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 82) A woman presents with painless vulval papillary growths. Application of 5% acetic acid turns the lesions white. The most likely diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: HPV-induced genital warts may become acetowhite after acetic acid application.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 83) A woman with recurrent PID complains of chronic pelvic pain. The underlying mechanism is most likely:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Repeated inflammation leads to adhesions, causing chronic pelvic pain.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 84) A pregnant woman presents with mucopurulent cervicitis due to Chlamydia trachomatis. The preferred treatment is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Azithromycin is safe and effective for chlamydial infection during pregnancy.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 85) A 28-year-old woman presents with lower abdominal pain, fever, and adnexal tenderness. Pregnancy test is negative. Ultrasound demonstrates a 7-cm tubo-ovarian abscess. Initial management should include:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Large tubo-ovarian abscesses require inpatient management with IV antibiotics, with drainage if necessary.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 86) A woman develops continuous urinary leakage 10 days after prolonged obstructed labor. Which investigation best confirms the diagnosis?
Genital Tract Infection.exp: The dye test is a simple bedside method for confirming vesicovaginal fistula.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 87) A 60-year-old woman with uterine prolapse has a pressure ulcer over the protruding cervix. The first step in management is:
Genital Tract Infection.option4: Local ulcer care before definitive surgery
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Decubitus ulcers should be treated before definitive prolapse surgery.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 88) A woman with urinary leakage only during coughing has a positive cough stress test. The diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Leakage during increased intra-abdominal pressure confirms stress incontinence.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 89) A woman with recurrent genital herpes asks where the virus remains latent between episodes. The correct answer is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: HSV establishes latency in the sacral sensory ganglia and reactivates periodically.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 90) A woman presents with a genital ulcer. Dark-field microscopy demonstrates motile spirochetes. The diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Dark-field microscopy demonstrating spirochetes is diagnostic of primary syphilis.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 91) A 35-year-old woman with severe pelvic organ prolapse desires future pregnancy. Which operation is most appropriate?
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Manchester operation preserves the uterus and may be considered in selected women desiring fertility.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 92) A woman with stress urinary incontinence undergoes urodynamic testing. Which finding is expected?
Genital Tract Infection.option1: Leakage during increased abdominal pressure without detrusor contraction
Genital Tract Infection.option4: Continuous leakage irrespective of bladder volume
Genital Tract Infection.exp: This is the characteristic urodynamic feature of stress urinary incontinence.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 93) A woman presents with fever, pelvic pain, and purulent cervical discharge. NAAT confirms gonorrhea. Which additional organism should empiric therapy routinely cover?
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Coinfection with chlamydia is common, so empiric treatment should cover both organisms.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 94) A woman with recurrent genital warts asks whether HPV vaccination is still beneficial. The best response is:
Genital Tract Infection.option1: Vaccination is only useful in men
Genital Tract Infection.option3: Vaccination can still provide protection against HPV types not yet acquired
Genital Tract Infection.exp: HPV vaccination does not treat existing infection but protects against additional HPV types.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 95) A woman develops fever, severe pelvic pain, rebound tenderness, and guarding. Which complication of PID should be suspected first?
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Rupture of a tubo-ovarian abscess is a life-threatening emergency causing generalized peritonitis.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 96) A woman with stage III uterine prolapse is unable to undergo surgery because of severe cardiac disease. The most appropriate long-term management is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: A pessary provides effective symptom relief in women unfit for surgery.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 97) A woman presents with painless genital ulcers that bleed easily on contact. Tissue smear demonstrates Donovan bodies. The diagnosis is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Donovan bodies are diagnostic of granuloma inguinale (donovanosis).

Genital Tract Infection.question: 98) A patient with severe PID is admitted for intravenous antibiotics. After 72 hours she is afebrile and improving clinically. The next appropriate step is:
Genital Tract Infection.option4: Switch to appropriate oral antibiotics to complete the recommended treatment course
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Clinical improvement allows transition to oral therapy to complete the full course.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 99) A woman with complete uterine prolapse develops bilateral hydronephrosis. The mechanism is:
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Advanced prolapse may obstruct the ureters, causing hydronephrosis.

Genital Tract Infection.question: 100) A 38-year-old multiparous woman presents with a vaginal bulge, urinary leakage on coughing, and difficulty emptying her bowel. Examination confirms uterine prolapse with cystocele and rectocele. She has completed childbearing and is medically fit. The most appropriate definitive management is:
Genital Tract Infection.option3: Vaginal hysterectomy with anterior and posterior colporrhaphy and pelvic floor repair
Genital Tract Infection.exp: Multicompartment pelvic organ prolapse in a woman who has completed childbearing is best managed with definitive reconstructive surgery.
